match.reason: The bank point teaches the same idea at a suitable depth for VCE Units 3 and 4: dynamic equilibrium in a closed system, with equal forward and reverse rates keeping amounts constant, and both of its questions are fair for Victorian students.

confirm.reason: The closest bank point covers dynamic equilibrium but also teaches static equilibrium as a separate idea, which NSW requires and the VCE study design does not, so it is broader than this point and a focused new card is safer.

draft.title: Dynamic equilibrium
card: A closed system lets energy move in or out, but no matter enters or leaves. In a closed system, a reversible reaction can reach equilibrium.
At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions both continue, and they go at equal rates.
Because the two rates are equal, each substance is made as fast as it is used up. Its amount and concentration stay constant, though they need not be equal to each other.
The equilibrium is dynamic, as particles keep reacting. It looks still on the large scale only. A reaction that has stopped would have no reactions at all.
draft.remember: At equilibrium, reactions keep going both ways at equal rates, so amounts stay constant.

a.q: What is the best reason the concentrations stay constant at equilibrium in a closed system?
opts: Forward and reverse reactions go on at equal rates
Both reactions have stopped, so nothing changes
The reactants and products have equal concentrations
The forward reaction has used up all the reactants
a.why: Each substance is made as fast as it is used up, so its concentration does not change. Constant concentrations do not mean the reactions have stopped, and they do not mean the concentrations are equal.
a.clue: Think about how fast each substance is made and used up.

b.q: Nitrogen dioxide gas in a sealed flask has reached equilibrium with dinitrogen tetroxide. The colour stops changing. Which statement about the flask is correct?
opts: Both reactions continue and their rates are equal
Neither reaction continues, as the colour is steady
Only the forward reaction continues, at a slower rate
The two gases are now present in equal concentrations
b.why: A steady colour shows the concentrations are constant, which happens when the forward and reverse rates are equal. It does not show the reactions have stopped, because particles keep reacting in both directions.
b.clue: A steady colour shows constant amounts, not a stopped reaction.

a.best: Forward and reverse reactions go on at equal rates

b.best: Both reactions continue and their rates are equal

problems.detail: The last sentence, 'A reaction that has stopped would have no reactions at all', is circular and confusing. It would be clearer as something like 'If the reaction had truly stopped, no particles would be reacting.'

check.summary: The facts and both questions are correct, and the intended answers match the explanations. The only issue is the circular final sentence on the card, which could be reworded for clarity.
